run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T09:32:04Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend-proxy RequestErrorRate alert corresponds to a ~2-minute burst of failed checkout requests at 09:22–09:24, not to a fault inside frontend-proxy. The payment Deployment in otel-demo was restarted in place at 2026-11-16T09:22:26Z (pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt, same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment, identical container spec). Because the payment container defines no readiness, liveness or startup probe, the Deployment treated the new pod as available the moment its container started (09:22:29) and scaled the old ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 to 0 at 09:22:29, while the new container did not log "payment gRPC server started on port 8080" until 09:23:44.571Z. The payment Service has a single endpoint, so for ~107 seconds the only endpoint was a process not yet listening. checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge client spans and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder spans errored only in the two 2-minute windows ending 09:24:00 and 09:25:00; frontend's POST /api/checkout / executing api route /api/checkout / grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder spans errored in the same windows; and frontend-proxy's own Envoy access log shows POST /api/checkout returning 500 via_upstream from 09:23:57 to 09:24:13 and 200 again from 09:24:17. That is the request-error signal behind the alert on frontend-proxy. A second, distinct and chronic population of frontend-proxy 503s (UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} on GET /api/*) exists both before and after the burst and is reported as an unresolved separate candidate. The alert rule itself is not loaded in the queried Prometheus, so its expression and the reported 0.022222 value and 09:32:04 onset could not be reproduced.

claims.text: The burst is short and sharply bounded: frontend-proxy 'ingress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans (2-minute increase) are 1.33 at 09:17:00, 1.33 at 09:20:00, 0 at 09:21:00–09:23:00, then 38.67 in the window ending 09:24:00 and 53.33 ending 09:25:00, and back to 1.598 at 09:26:00, 1.333 at 09:29:00, 2.667 at 09:32:00, 2.803 at 09:33:00 and 0–2.667 through 09:39:00.

The 16-minute-window readings that look like a 15-minute plateau are window overlap: frontend-proxy ingress STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase over [16m] reads 38.19 at 09:24:04, 76.39 at 09:27:04, 78.45 at 09:33:04–09:36:04 and 51.83 at 09:39:04, then 9.41/8.49/4.35 at 09:42:04/09:45:04/09:48:04, i.e. the same short burst sliding out of the 16-minute range selector.

checkout's dependency spans fail only in those same two 2-minute windows: oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder show 54.67 error spans at 09:24:00 and 54.67 at 09:25:00 and 0 at every other point from 09:16:00 to 09:39:00; frontend spans POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder show 37.33 at 09:24:00 and 54.67 at 09:25:00 and 0 elsewhere.

Over the 50 minutes ending 09:25:00, checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge client spans total 51.98 STATUS_CODE_ERROR against 823.56 STATUS_CODE_UNSET, i.e. the failed charge calls are concentrated in the burst.

The payment Deployment spec carries pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T09:22:26Z, replicas 1, strategy RollingUpdate with maxSurge 25% / maxUnavailable 25%, and its container has no readinessProbe, no livenessProbe and no startupProbe (port 8080/tcp only).

Kubernetes events show a controller-driven rollout of payment, not a crash: pod payment-54499f9786-4r25d Scheduled 09:22:26Z, container payment Started 09:22:29Z; Deployment payment 'Scaled up replica set payment-54499f9786 from 0 to 1' at 09:22:26Z and 'Scaled down replica set payment-55766d76b9 from 1 to 0' at 09:22:29Z; ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete and 'Stopping container payment' on old pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 at 09:22:29Z.

Both payment ReplicaSets use the identical image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment with identical env, resources (limits cpu 20m / memory 160Mi) and no probes: payment-54499f9786 (revision 2, created 2026-11-16T09:22:26Z) and payment-55766d76b9 (revision 1, created 2026-11-16T08:50:14Z, now replicas 0).

The new payment container was silent and not serving for over a minute after the old pod was removed: its first readable log line is "payment gRPC server started on port 8080" at 2026-11-16T09:23:44.571Z, and its first "Charge request received." is at 09:24:17.971Z.

checkout's application log matches the gap: "payment went through"/"order placed" pairs continue until 09:22:29.762, then from 09:22:30.287 to 09:23:57.207 every line is a bare "[PlaceOrder]" with no payment/order line, and successful "payment went through"/"order placed" pairs appear again from 09:26:04.713 onward.

The payment Service is a ClusterIP on port 8080 selecting opentelemetry.io/name=payment, and its Endpoints contain exactly one address, the new pod payment-54499f9786-4r25d at 100.96.5.201, so the rollout swapped a single endpoint.

All 21 pods in otel-demo are Running and ready with restartCount 0; frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-sznks started 2026-11-16T08:50:14Z (same as its siblings) while payment-54499f9786-4r25d started 09:22:26Z, so only payment was replaced during the incident window.

payment itself is not the failing component after startup: its own error-status span series (span names GET, dns.lookup, tcp.connect) are 0 for the whole 09:03–09:48 window, and its logs from 09:33:37 to 09:36:23 contain only alternating "Charge request received."/"Transaction complete." lines.

A separate, chronic error population exists at frontend-proxy on GET traffic: Envoy logged "503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}" for GET /api/recommendations, /api/products/* and /api/data/?contextKeys=* at 09:01:35, 09:09:20, 09:10:07, 09:13:00, 09:14:03, 09:15:20 and 09:18:24, and the 09:00–09:20 trace sample shows frontend-proxy ingress spans with error=true, http.status_code=503, otel.status_code=ERROR whose child 'router frontend egress' span has error="true", http.status_code="0" and no frontend span beneath it.

The chronic 503 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' GET failures are a second, independent contributor to frontend-proxy's error rate that precedes the payment restart and persists after the burst (ingress error increases of 8.49 and 4.35 per 16 minutes at 09:45:04 and 09:48:04). They are not caused by the payment rollout, and how much of the alert's 0.022222 ratio they account for cannot be separated without the alert expression.

frontend-proxy's own health signals do not explain the burst: its pod has restartCount 0 and has been running since 08:50:14, and its CFS throttling ratio stayed flat at 0.0960/0.0858/0.0859/0.0935/0.0907/0.0856/0.0910/0.0971 across 09:02–09:37 (0.195 at 09:42), while the failing responses in the burst are 500 via_upstream, i.e. produced by the frontend upstream rather than by the proxy itself.

A payment image/code change was considered and rejected: both payment ReplicaSets run the same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment with identical env, resources and absent probes, so the 09:22:26 rollout changed only the pod-template restart annotation.

A payment pod crash, OOM or eviction was considered and rejected: restartCount is 0, the events are the controller's own SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete/ScalingReplicaSet for the rollout, there is no previous container instance for the new pod, and the new pod logged successful charges shortly after starting.

Add a readinessProbe (and a startupProbe with a startup budget) on port 8080 for the payment container and set the rolling update to maxUnavailable: 0, so the old payment pod is not removed until the new one actually accepts connections; the ~75 s gap between container start (09:22:29) and "payment gRPC server started on port 8080" (09:23:44.571) also suggests the cpu limit of 20m is too small for a single-replica service's startup.

Retrieve the RequestErrorRate alert rule/Alertmanager configuration and confirm whether it counts HTTP 4xx/5xx request outcomes or span status codes and over which window; only then can the reported 0.022222 ratio and the 09:32:04 alert start be reconciled with the observed 09:23:57–09:24:13 error burst.

gaps: The alert rule is not available: list_prometheus_rules for rule_name RequestErrorRate returned no_data, and the queried Prometheus exposes only trace-derived and container/runtime metrics (63 names, no http_server_*, rpc_client_* or kube_* series), so the alert's PromQL expression, its metric, its evaluation window/for and the reported current value 0.02222222222222222 cannot be verified or reproduced, and the ~8-minute gap between the last observed request error (09:24:13) and the alert start (09:32:04) is unexplained.

No kube-state-metrics series exist here (kube_* absent from the metric list; kube_pod_container_info for payment returned no_data), so image digests could not be compared via metrics and kube_deployment_status_replicas_available/ready could not be read; image identity was taken from the ReplicaSet specs instead.

Jaeger data for the requested windows ends at about 09:15–09:17 and the 30-trace frontend-proxy query was refused as RESULT_TOO_LARGE, so no trace covers the 09:22–09:24 burst; the exact gRPC status code payment returned to checkout (UNAVAILABLE / connection refused / deadline) and a trace-confirmed parent-child edge for the failing charges are unknown.

The frontend container produced no readable log lines for 09:22:00–09:25:30 (fetch returned no_data, 0 lines), so its internal handling of /api/checkout is visible only as Envoy's 500 via_upstream response.

Events returned only 9 Normal events dated 09:22:26–09:22:29 and the Warning-type filter returned no_data; the absence of other warnings (probe failures, evictions, OOMKilled) is not established because events expire and the window's earlier events were not returned.

Log coverage is truncated for the affected pods: the payment log has no previous instance and its readable stream ends at 09:36:23.957, so nothing from the terminated old pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 or from later than that is available; the frontend-proxy log stream hit the 4 MiB read limit at 09:20:32 in one query.
No change_history integration is available, so who or what issued the rollout restart (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T09:22:26Z) on the payment Deployment cannot be established.

The cause of the chronic 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} responses on GET /api/* (frontend terminating the connection before response start) is unknown; frontend logs were unavailable for that period and no frontend-side status other than 200 appears in its spans.
next_steps: Read the RequestErrorRate rule and Alertmanager route to confirm the expression, window and the 0.0222 current value, and confirm whether HTTP 5xx from the frontend counts as a frontend-proxy request error.
Review who ran the payment rollout restart at 2026-11-16T09:22:26Z using the change-history/CI system once that integration is available.
Add a readiness/startup probe and maxUnavailable: 0 to the payment Deployment and reassess its 20m CPU limit so a single-replica pod can be serving before its predecessor is removed.
Investigate the pre-existing GET /api/* 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} pattern with frontend-side telemetry over a period Jaeger still holds.
